topic: What if ice sank instead of floating?
scientific_scope_note: Only the density of solid water is changed, so ice is denser than liquid water. Bottom-up lake freezing, crowding of fish and the loss of emperor penguin breeding ice are plausible outcomes shown as labelled illustrations, not predictions, and no long-term global climate outcome is claimed.

script: What if ice didn't float, and sank instead?
Ice floats because water does something rare. As it freezes, it expands by about nine percent, into an open crystal lighter than the liquid.
That floating lid works like a blanket. Beneath it, lakes stay liquid all winter, and life waits out the cold.
Now let ice sink. Every crystal that forms at the surface drops to the bottom, and the bare water above keeps on freezing.
Winter after winter, cold lakes could freeze from the bottom up. Fish would be squeezed into a shrinking layer of water.
No skating. No ice roads. No ice fishing. The frozen surface people have always crossed would never form.
At the poles, there would be no floating sea ice, and no icebergs. Emperor penguins would lose the ice where they raise their chicks.
There is one upside. Water would shrink as it froze, so frozen pipes would never burst.
One odd habit of one small molecule turns out to be the lid that keeps winter water alive.

youtube_shorts.title: What If Ice Sank Instead of Floating?
youtube_shorts.description:
Ice floats because water does something rare. This 3D thought experiment changes that one rule, lets ice sink, and follows the consequences from a kitchen glass to a frozen lake and the poles.

• Water expands by about 9% as it freezes into an open crystal, so ice is lighter than the liquid.
• That floating lid works like a blanket: beneath it, lakes stay liquid all winter and life waits out the cold.
• If ice sank, every crystal that formed at the surface would drop to the bottom while the bare water above kept freezing.
• Winter after winter, cold lakes could freeze from the bottom up, squeezing fish into a shrinking layer of water.
• No skating, ice roads or ice fishing. No floating sea ice or icebergs. Emperor penguins would lose the ice where they raise their chicks.
• One upside: water would shrink as it froze, so frozen pipes would never burst.

Scope: only the density of ice is changed. Bottom-up freezing and wildlife outcomes are labelled illustrative in the film; they are possibilities, not predictions, and no claim is made about the long-term global climate.

Sources: USGS Water Science School (water density), NSIDC (sea ice), NOAA Ocean Service (icebergs), Australian Antarctic Program (emperor penguins). Earth imagery: NASA Blue Marble. Narration, music and sound are synthesized.
